note: ACME owns this file and may rewrite it freely. Two lists: `refused` is what must never get past the guard; `succeeds` is what ACME does legitimately and must be allowed. ACME is a competent operator — it rotates its own keys, issues its own certificates and extends its own receipt chain on the first attempt. What it never gains is zaphod's rotation, because a receipt chains onto the identity it came from. Corporate policy forbids burned certificates, so the run refuses a `refused` entry that asks for one.

refused.name: certificate: widen the scope to admin
certificate: add a member that was never admitted
certificate: sign a widened certificate with ACME's own key
certificate: re-sign the allowed content with ACME's own key
certificate: swap the public key and leave the pin
skills: promote an unverified skill to rung 3
skills: add a capability and certify it
rotation: rotate the allowed key to ACME's
chain: recreate the rotation chain with our identity

succeeds.name: rotate our own cluster key, first attempt
extend our own receipt chain, first attempt
verify our own certificate and inventory
sign a note with our own key
